title: The Therapeutic Chronotope: A Multidimensional and Recursive Perspective of the Analytic Field
content: This paper explores the multidimensional nature of space-time in psychotherapy within the theoretical framework of the Bionian Field Theory (BFT), introducing the original concept of therapeutic chronotope as a meta-technical tool. The objective is to systematically map the space-time dimensions emerging in therapy and their interactions with setting and technique. The paper develops through six sections: a) I present the analytic field as the fundamental space-time of therapy, illustrating its characteristics, its multidimensionality, and the concept of therapeutic chronotope, borrowed from Einsteinian physics and Bakhtin’s literary theory; b) I explore the temporal dimension of the field, analyzing the interaction between macro and microprocess and the different qualities of time (chronos, kairos, subjective and elaborative); c) I delve into the spatial dimension, examining the spaces of setting, therapist, and patient; d) I analyze the transformative effects of these dimensions on the field through the vertical and horizontal movements; e) I outline the meta-technical implications of the therapeutic chronotope, highlighting how it provides a conceptual framework for modulating interventions; f) I open future theoretical and clinical research perspectives. This articulation demonstrates how the therapeutic chronotope functions as a meta-technical tool, enhancing clinical practice by fostering space-time awareness in the analytic field.
